## TL;DR

Updated Mission Control and Stories to use one representative skeleton block each, so neither page sprouts placeholder rows at wide widths. Added a shared shell delay/minimum-visible interval, route coverage and skeleton shape tests, reduced-motion coverage, and deterministic loading fixtures for both pages. The UI verification round 1 identified that forced loading shots omitted `aria-busy`; this fix restores it and defines the shots through the registered fixture `state` field so verification can capture the intentional loading state.

## Work and rationale

Mission Control is a continuous dashboard of usage, system resources, status counts, feed and other panels. A six-card auto-fit skeleton was structurally wrong and wrapped at wide widths. Its replacement uses one full-width block. Stories renders story cards in a single vertical list, so its loading state uses one representative row rather than five invented rows. Static page heading chrome stays outside the placeholder. The shared skeleton component exposes a single polite status and honors reduced motion.

The route-level shell waits 180 ms before showing a placeholder and keeps a shown placeholder for at least 350 ms. This prevents a fast initial response from flashing a skeleton. The fake-timer tests cover the fast-load and minimum-visible cases. The new fixtures, `loading:dashboard` and `loading:stories`, pin the shell into the loading state for declared screenshots.

The route/layout audit covered the current route map and per-view skeleton call sites:

| Page | Real shape | Skeleton shape | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mission Control | Stacked dashboard sections and status strip | One wide dashboard block | Corrected |
| Work | Status columns; one column at narrow breakpoint | Work column count from shared constant | Matches |
| Client board / Inputs | Three workflow columns | Input column count from shared constant | Matches |
| Stories | Vertical list of story cards | One representative list row | Corrected |
| Checks | Plan and run tables | Table rows | Matches |
| Releases | Release cards and distribution history | Card placeholders / table panel | Matches |
| Deployments | Environment by branch matrix | Summary cards and matrix | Matches |
| Dev | Declared target cards | Target placeholders | Matches |
| Secrets | Key/value table | Table rows | Matches |
| Agents | Agent and budget cards | Card placeholders | Matches |
| Settings | Configuration panels and rows | Rows | Matches |
| Repo | Context/document sections | Rows | Matches |

The board item counts follow the same constants as their rendered content. Each skeleton kind has a count assertion based on its declared layout definition; CSS under `prefers-reduced-motion` disables animation and has a regression assertion.

## Approaches tried

I inspected the page markup and route mapping before changing the skeleton. Restricting the dashboard grid with overflow or adjusting its card width would still have left it looking like unrelated cards. The single-block representation better matches the dashboard's uninterrupted stack and avoids wrapping. Stories uses the same minimum-placeholder principle for its list.

The capture tool intentionally rejects screenshots that show `aria-busy` or another loading signal, because those captures can also indicate a page that never finished mounting. The owner updated acceptance criterion 6 to remove loading-state screenshots and make skeleton structure/count tests the evidence for the loading UI. I cleared the loading-state shot declarations with `repoos update 1070 --shots '[]'` and restored the verifier's unconditional loading-state check. The round 1 accessibility finding remains addressed: forced loading fixtures and real delayed skeletons both mark their region `aria-busy`, and the App template test asserts this attribute.

## Challenges and blockers

The shell loader and per-view skeletons are reached through different loading signals. The shared initial shell timing is centralized and tested; view-level data loading retains existing cached-data guards so background refreshes do not replace visible content. Loading screenshots conflict with the verifier's settled-page evidence contract, so the accepted scope relies on component tests for skeleton shape and item counts; no loading-state shots are declared.

## Key learnings

Skeletons should be checked against their real page at the largest viewport, where auto-fit layouts can expose stray placeholder rows. Route-to-skeleton mapping tests alone do not validate visual shape; item count and reduced-motion assertions add useful guards. Loading-state views should keep their accessible busy marker, while screenshot evidence should use settled pages because the capture gate treats a visible busy marker as a failed capture.
